title: Multivariate outlier detector + adaptive alert throttling for console telemetry
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a resilient, low-noise anomaly detection and alerting pipeline for Console usage/cost/latency telemetry that can detect multivariate degradations (e.g., cost spike + P95 latency shift on a route) and surface actionable root-cause signals to SREs and account owners. The scope covers streaming feature extraction, real-time detection, aggregation/grouping rules, an adaptive alert throttling layer, and a runbook integration for on-call.

Background: Current alerts are primarily single-metric threshold-based and generate a high volume of false positives when traffic patterns change (region deployments, marketing spikes). We need a production-capable detector that balances sensitivity against operational noise and ties anomalies to likely causes (model change, rollout, infra region, customer cohort).

Design summary and chosen approach:
- Data plane: reuse existing Kafka topic console.telemetry.v1 for ingest. Use a Flink job (scalable event-time windowing) for streaming feature extraction and online scoring. Batch re-training and feature validation will run in Dataproc weekly.
- Features: per-route and per-account time series: token_rate, req_rate, p50/p95/p99 latency, avg_cost_per_token, error_rate, concurrency. Also engineered multivariate features: latency_cost_ratio, short-term gradient (last 5m), normalized seasonality residual (weekly baseline subtraction).
- Detection models: hybrid ensemble
  1) Robust univariate detectors per metric: rolling MAD-based z-score with dynamic window (1h/6h) and seasonality-aware baseline for quick detection of sudden spikes.
  2) Multivariate streaming isolation-forest-lite (incremental sketching) to catch joint shifts that univariate checks miss.
  3) Gradient detector: a lightweight exponential-weighted slope test to detect rapid growth (helps flag bursts early).
  Ensemble decision: majority vote + weighted severity score (higher weight for p95 latency and cost anomalies). A confidence score is emitted for downstream routing.
- Grouping & deduplication: anomalies are grouped by (org_id, project_id, route, model_variant) and by correlated metrics. We coalesce events within a 10m window to avoid alert storms.
- Adaptive alert throttling & escalation policy:
  - Tier 1: automated pager when anomaly confidence >= 0.9 AND customer_impact == high OR SLOs breached.
  - Tier 2: Slack alert to #console-alerts for confidence 0.6-0.9 with attached diagnostics.
  - Throttle: exponential backoff per group with token-bucket resets after anomaly resolution or 1h of stability.
  - Noise suppression: require anomalies to persist for at least two detection windows (configurable) unless severity is critical.
- Explainability & triage hints: attach top contributing features (SHAP-lite approximation for the isolation-forest) and recent deployment/GitHub PR metadata (via a lightweight join against deployments.index) to help root-cause.

Trade-offs considered:
- Compute cost vs. recall: Running a full isolation forest per org is expensive. We use a sketching approach and fall back to univariate detectors for low-traffic orgs. This reduces CPU/GPU cost but slightly lowers multivariate sensitivity for small tenants.
- Black-box vs explainable: We prioritized explainability for on-call UX; therefore we avoided deep ensemble models requiring heavy feature stores and opted for interpretable feature contributions.
- Streaming consistency vs latency: Event-time windows (Flink) provide correct ordering for delayed events but add 30-60s wait. We accepted this to avoid false positives from out-of-order telemetry.

Operational requirements & SLAs:
- Detector job must be horizontally autoscalable; aim P50 processing latency < 30s, P95 < 90s for anomaly detection end-to-end from event ingestion.
- Alert delivery success rate > 99.5% to Slack/pager service. Circuit-breaker and fallback to email for downstream delivery failures.

Runbook & playbook integration:
- When an alert fires, the message includes: summary, confidence, contributing metrics, top-k correlated orgs/routes, recent deployments (last 24h), and link to the pre-populated runbook.
- Escalation steps: triage (SRE), confirm degradation, rollback or mitigate, run evals on suspect model version, open incident if customer-facing.

Future enhancements (non-blocking): labeling by root-cause using downstream SR and incident datasets to train a small classifier for automated root_cause suggestions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Real-time anomaly events emitted to topic console.anomalies.v1 with schema {group_key, timestamp, metrics, confidence, top_contribs, suggested_action}.
- Dashboard showing precision/recall estimates for synthetic injected anomalies and historical alert noise rate < 25% by week-3 after rollout.
- Integrations: Slack, PagerDuty, Console Incidents service.

Notes on data schema and privacy: payloads must not contain PII. We will hash account IDs (salted) in analytics views and only include org_id unhashed in internal services.
comments: 2025-02-19: Kickoff meeting - agreed on Flink as streaming engine and isolation-forest-lite for joint anomalies. Action: Marco to draft detection prototypes.
2025-02-24: PM feedback (Hannah Lee) - add explicit SLO tie-in for alerting; updated policy to require SLO breach override for pagers.
2025-02-27: Design review (Jun Park) - suggested alert message UX with inline triage links; added runbook templating to scope.

2025-03-02: Engineering update - prototype running on a sampled Kafka topic with univariate MAD checks; false-positive rate reduced vs current alerts. Next: integrate multivariate scorer and grouping logic.

2025-03-04: Security note from Compliance (R. Gomez) - confirm hashing scheme for org IDs and add config toggle to disable cross-org correlation for customers in high-reg sectors. Marking security_review_required=false but will add follow-up ticket if needed.
